guarantees.claim: fifo_rready_o equals sha_rready_i when HMAC is disabled; when HMAC enabled, it equals (st_q == StMsg) & sha_rready_i.
sha_rvalid_o equals fifo_rvalid_i when HMAC is disabled, and equals hmac_sha_rvalid when HMAC is enabled.
sha_rdata_o equals fifo_rdata_i when HMAC is disabled.
sha_rdata_o equals '{data: i_pad_256[(BlockSizeSHA256-1)-32*pad_index_256-:32], mask: '1} when HMAC enabled, sel_rdata selects IPad, and digest is SHA-256.
sha_rdata_o equals '{data: i_pad_512[(BlockSizeSHA512-1)-32*pad_index_512-:32], mask: '1} when HMAC enabled, sel_rdata selects IPad, and digest is SHA-384 or SHA-512.
guarantees.cond: hmac_en_i && sel_rdata == SelIPad && (digest_size_i == SHA2_384 || digest_size_i == SHA2_512)

guarantees.claim: sha_rdata_o equals '{data: o_pad_256[(BlockSizeSHA256-1)-32*pad_index_256-:32], mask: '1} when HMAC enabled, sel_rdata selects OPad, and digest is SHA-256.
sha_rdata_o equals '{data: o_pad_512[(BlockSizeSHA512-1)-32*pad_index_512-:32], mask: '1} when HMAC enabled, sel_rdata selects OPad, and digest is SHA-384 or SHA-512.
guarantees.cond: hmac_en_i && sel_rdata == SelOPad && (digest_size_i == SHA2_384 || digest_size_i == SHA2_512)

guarantees.claim: sha_rdata_o equals fifo_rdata_i for any other combination when HMAC enabled, including SelFifo and any illegal sel_rdata values.
guarantees.cond: hmac_en_i && (sel_rdata not in {SelIPad,SelOPad} or does not match a pad case) – default case

assumptions.claim: pad_index_256 must stay within [0, BlockSizeSHA256/32) to guarantee in-bounds read from i_pad_256 and o_pad_256 arrays.
assumptions.cond: when sel_rdata == SelIPad or SelOPad and digest_size_i == SHA2_256
assumptions.risk: Out‑of‑bounds read may return X or wrong data, silently corrupting HMAC ipad/opad insertion and compromising authentication.

assumptions.claim: pad_index_512 must stay within [0, BlockSizeSHA512/32) to guarantee in-bounds read from i_pad_512 and o_pad_512 arrays.
assumptions.cond: when sel_rdata == SelIPad or SelOPad and (digest_size_i == SHA2_384 or SHA2_512)
assumptions.risk: Out‑of‑bounds read may return X or wrong data, silently corrupting HMAC ipad/opad insertion and compromising authentication.

assumptions.claim: The pad arrays i_pad_256, i_pad_512, o_pad_256, o_pad_512 are pre‑loaded with the correct HMAC inner/outer pad words.
assumptions.cond: when HMAC enabled and sel_rdata selects a pad source
assumptions.risk: Incorrect pad values lead to a wrong HMAC result, either failing authentication or creating a security bypass.

assumptions.claim: When sel_rdata == SelIPad or SelOPad, st_q is not StMsg (i.e., HMAC is not in the message‑streaming phase), so pad data is not mixed with message data flow.
assumptions.risk: Pad data could be injected as message data, corrupting the HMAC state and possibly exposing internal pad values.

uncertain_points.claim: If pad_index_256 or pad_index_512 is out‑of‑range, the multiplexer still uses the index to read the pad arrays, potentially delivering X or corrupted pad words to the SHA engine. No local range check or error flag exists inside this chunk.
uncertain_points.cond: HMAC pad phase with out‑of‑range pad index
uncertain_points.risk: Silent corruption of HMAC pad data, leading to false authentication, and no containment of the fault.

uncertain_points.claim: The sha_rdata_o multiplexer does not verify that sel_rdata is only asserted during a safe state; it relies on the external HMAC FSM to ensure sel_rdata is never SelIPad/SelOPad while st_q == StMsg.
uncertain_points.risk: If an FSM bug asserts pad selection during the message phase, pad data could be passed as SHA input, corrupting the HMAC computation.
